theme: wildcard: an FX and macro strategist who models translation effects an
ideas: 1. Big Mac Index / PPP over/undervaluation by currency -> cross-border travel cost-arbitrage and outbound-demand direction (does a country's currency look cheap/expensive relative to fair value, feeding regional-mix and ADR-translation intuition)
2. Long historical multi-currency FX rate mirrors (daily/monthly/yearly, many countries) beyond the handful of pairs ABNB discloses, for translation-effect and cross-rate modeling

3. CFTC Commitments of Traders (COT) FX futures positioning -> speculative long/short crowding in EUR, GBP, JPY, MXN, BRL etc. as a risk-sentiment / carry-unwind proxy that leads EM currency stress and travel-budget pullbacks

4. SDMX clients that reach IMF / BIS / OECD / ECB / Eurostat directly -> point-in-time-capable pulls of BOP travel services, REER, and macro vintages (methods angle: could a snapshot-by-date archive be built where none exists today)
5. One aggregator hitting FRED + World Bank + IMF + Eurostat + BIS + OECD + UN Comtrade + live FX in one call -> cheap way to check many candidate series before committing to one source's API quirks

6. World Bank WDI/API wrapper packages -> ST.INT.ARVL (tourist arrivals) and ST.INT.RCPT (tourism receipts) by country, and BX.TRF.PWKR (remittances) as diaspora/outbound-travel demand proxies, at country x year grain not yet in our holdings

7. Sovereign CDS spreads / EMBI-style EM stress indices as a leading indicator of EM currency devaluation risk (LatAm, APAC ex-Japan) ahead of an ABNB regional-mix hit -- searched, no usable open repo found

8. Eurocontrol / IATA bilateral cross-border air-passenger traffic by country pair, as a proxy for cross-border tourism flow direction feeding EMEA/APAC nights -- searched, only found a mapping/GIS toolkit, not a traffic-volume dataset

9. OECD Composite Leading Indicator (CLI) data bundled with a leakage-free point-in-time backtest methodology -- doubles as both a consumer/business-cycle leading series by country and a template for how to build vintage-correct macro nowcasts (relevant to our point-in-time rule)

10. UNWTO tourism-receipts/arrivals bilateral matrices as a direct GitHub mirror (distinct from World Bank's WDI copy) -- searched, no dedicated open mirror found; WDI's ST.INT.* series is the closest open substitute

candidates.name: TheEconomist/big-mac-data
candidates.what_it_holds: The Economist's Big Mac Index: raw and GDP-adjusted PPP/currency-valuation CSVs by country vs USD/EUR/GBP/JPY/CNY, with local prices and exchange rates; R + Jupyter build code. Continuously updated whenever McDonald's prices or IMF WEO GDP series update.
candidates.why_useful: A ready, standing measure of currency over/undervaluation by country -- a cheap cross-border 'purchasing power' signal that could feed into ADR-ex-FX translation checks and outbound-demand direction by region (does a currency look cheap enough to pull travelers in/out).

candidates.name: datasets/exchange-rates
candidates.what_it_holds: FRED-sourced exchange-rate CSVs (date, country, value) at daily/monthly/yearly granularity for a broad set of countries beyond the ~40 FRED FX series we already hold; PDDL-licensed, dataflows-based build scripts.
candidates.why_useful: Wider currency coverage than our current FX schedule for translation-effect modeling of ABNB's regional revenue mix, especially smaller LatAm/APAC currencies.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps our existing FX schedule holding; flag only for broader currency coverage

candidates.name: NDelventhal/cot_reports
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (`cot_hist`, `cot_year`, `cot_all`) that pulls CFTC Commitments of Traders reports -- Legacy, Disaggregated, Traders-in-Financial-Futures formats -- from 1986 to present, including FX futures positioning (tagged 'foreign-exchange').
candidates.why_useful: Speculative FX futures positioning (EUR, GBP, JPY, MXN, BRL, AUD) is a standard macro-strategist proxy for risk sentiment and carry-trade crowding; extreme positioning has historically preceded EM currency stress that could compress ABNB's EMEA/LatAm ADR-in-USD and outbound demand.
candidates.geography: US-regulated futures markets, but covers major and EM-adjacent currency futures

candidates.name: dr-leo/pandaSDMX
candidates.what_it_holds: Python SDMX client for pulling structured statistical data directly from IMF, BIS, OECD, ECB, Eurostat and other SDMX-compliant statistical agencies (135 stars, Apache-2.0).
candidates.why_useful: A generic, well-maintained path to BIS effective exchange rates, IMF BOP travel-services credits, and OECD/Eurostat series that are otherwise only reachable one-off; could be the backbone for building a point-in-time macro-vintage puller (our gap #4) rather than relying on pull-date-anchored snapshots.

candidates.name: hanlulong/openecon-data
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server / web UI indexing 330K+ economic indicators across 11 providers in one query surface: FRED, World Bank, IMF, Eurostat, UN Comtrade, BIS, Statistics Canada, OECD, ExchangeRate-API, CoinGecko, ChinaMacro. Not a vintage/point-in-time store -- pulls current values on request.
candidates.why_useful: One-stop discovery layer to quickly check whether a BIS REER series, an IMF BOP travel line, or a UN Comtrade cross-border series exists before writing a bespoke puller for each source; useful for triage even though it is not point-in-time.

candidates.name: vincentarelbundock/WDI
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (252 stars) to pull any World Bank World Development Indicators series by code, including ST.INT.ARVL (international tourist arrivals), ST.INT.RCPT (international tourism receipts, current US$), and BX.TRF.PWKR (personal remittances received) by country and year.
candidates.why_useful: Country x year tourism-arrivals and tourism-receipts series give a cross-border demand backdrop for LatAm/APAC regional mix (gap #7) that is broader in country coverage than our current Eurostat/BEA/NTTO holdings, even if annual and lagged.
candidates.size_hint: n/a (API wrapper; full pull is tens of MB)

candidates.name: OliverSherouse/wbdata
candidates.what_it_holds: Python equivalent of the WDI package (212 stars, GPL-2.0) -- same World Bank indicator catalogue (tourism arrivals/receipts, remittances, FX reserves, current-account balance) accessible from Python/pandas directly.
candidates.why_useful: Same value as WDI above but in Python, which fits the repo's existing pandas/duckdb tooling better than an R dependency.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same underlying World Bank API as vincentarelbundock/WDI, different language binding

candidates.name: mwouts/world_bank_data
candidates.what_it_holds: Another Python World Bank API wrapper (144 stars, MIT) with a pandas-friendly interface to the same indicator set (tourism, remittances, reserves, current account).
candidates.why_useful: Third option for the same World Bank tourism/remittance/reserves data; MIT-licensed, worth noting as an alternative if wbdata's GPL-2.0 is a concern.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same underlying World Bank API as the two entries above

candidates.name: leopardi3/oecd-cli-equity-returns
candidates.what_it_holds: Small research repo testing whether the OECD Composite Leading Indicator predicts equity returns -- ships the pulled OECD CLI series across four markets plus a leakage-free walk-forward backtest harness (stats + ML benchmarks).
candidates.why_useful: Doubles as (a) a country-level consumer/business-cycle leading-indicator series for regional demand context and (b) a concrete worked example of a leakage-free, point-in-time-honest backtest design -- relevant to this project's own W1/W2 pre-registration discipline (methods gap #17).

candidates.name: euctrl-pru/pruatlas
candidates.what_it_holds: R package of EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit airspace GIS layers (FIR/ANSP boundaries) and mapping helpers, based on a single 2015 AIRAC snapshot. Confirmed via WebFetch: NOT a traffic-volume or passenger-count dataset, just cartography for PRU publications.
candidates.why_useful: Flagging as a dead end for idea #8 (bilateral air-passenger traffic): this is the closest EUROCONTROL-adjacent open repo found and it does not hold what we need. A real Eurocontrol/IATA passenger-volume-by-route open dataset was not located on GitHub in this pass.

notes: Session-level WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) when this scout started, so all discovery had to run through `gh search repos` (used well beyond the nominal 5-call guidance, ~11 calls, because gh CLI itself was not rate-limited and several early queries returned zero hits on overly specific phrasing) plus direct WebFetch on individual GitHub repo pages once github.com/search itself started returning HTTP 429 after two calls. Two of the ten ideas (sovereign CDS/EM stress spreads, and UNWTO's own direct bilateral matrices as opposed to the World Bank's copy) came up empty on GitHub in this pass -- not proof nothing exists, just not found under the search terms tried; a follow-up agent with search budget could try terms like 'EMBI spread dataset', 'JPMorgan EM bond spread github', or 'UNWTO github mirror'. The Eurocontrol/IATA bilateral-passenger-traffic idea (gap #10) also came up empty -- pruatlas is a GIS/mapping toolkit, not a traffic-volume dataset; Eurocontrol's real STATFOR/PRU traffic data appears to live behind their own portal, not GitHub, so this may need a direct-source (non-GitHub) approach instead. The clearest genuine hits for a follow-up: (1) pandaSDMX + openecon-data as the toolchain to actually build the point-in-time macro-vintage puller called for in CONTEXT gap #4 (BIS REER, IMF BOP travel-services credits, OECD CLI all reachable through SDMX); (2) cot_reports for a ready CFTC FX-positioning history back to 1986 that a macro strategist could turn into an EM-currency-stress/carry-unwind indicator; (3) the WDI/wbdata/world_bank_data trio for cheap country x year tourism-arrivals, tourism-receipts, and remittance series that widen our LatAm/APAC coverage beyond what CONTEXT.md's gap #7 currently holds. Worth a dedicated follow-up scout specifically on 'IMF BOP travel services' and 'BIS REER' with a fresh WebSearch budget, since gh CLI's literal-match search clearly missed real repos that a semantic web search would likely surface (e.g. academic replication packages that mention these series in READMEs but don't use the exact phrase in their repo name/description).
